explanation: Erdős #161: how does F^{(t)}(n, α) change as α goes from 0 to 1/2 (continuously, jumps, one jump)? It is formalized as determining, for each t, the set of pairs (α, β) in [0, 1/2)² with F^{(t)}(n, α) ≍ F^{(t)}(n, β). That is a reasonable precise reading of "jumps in growth order". The site notes the t = 3 case is resolved (only one jump, at α = 0, by Conlon–Fox–Sudakov), but general t remains open. The statement is faithful and open.
